spec: The SDX Protocol deterministic encoding profile, with its shortest-form integer rule. Each vector pins the hex-encoded canonical CBOR bytes for a known input, computed via cbor-x 1.6.4 with the canonical-profile options (useRecords:false, variableMapSize:true, mapsAsObjects:false, tagUint8Array:false, useFloat32:0, alwaysUseFloat:false, bundleStrings:false) plus repo-side normalisation (sorted-by-canonical-key-bytes carried as a Map<string,V>, safe integers needing an 8-byte head widened to BigInt so cbor-x emits major-type-0/1 rather than float64, Date to ms-int, Set to sorted-array, Map input sorted by key bytes, undefined-elision). A bigint INPUT is refused outright (profile rule, fixed 2026-08-11), so bigints appear here only as an internal widening, never as a vector input.

vectors.name: empty-map
vectors.doc: RFC 8949 §3.2.1: empty map encodes to 0xa0 (major-type 5, length 0)

vectors.name: single-key-map
vectors.doc: Single string key 'a' (1 byte UTF-8) -> integer 1

vectors.name: sorted-multi-key-map-from-insertion-order
vectors.doc: Insertion order {b,a,c} canonicalises to bytewise key order {a,b,c}. Each key is one byte (0x6161, 0x6162, 0x6163), so canonical sort is equivalent to lexicographic sort over the keys.

vectors.name: byte-sort-not-string-sort
vectors.doc: Keys 'aaa' (3-byte UTF-8 prefix tag 0x63 + bytes) and 'z' (1-byte tag 0x61 + byte). Bytewise CBOR-key order: 0x61 < 0x63, so 'z' sorts before 'aaa'. JS UTF-16 sort would give the opposite. Locks the encoder to RFC 8949 §4.2.1 bytewise ordering.

vectors.name: nested-map
vectors.doc: Outer map with one key 'outer' (5 chars) -> inner map {z:1, a:2}. Inner keys also sort bytewise (a < z).

vectors.name: long-string-23-bytes
vectors.doc: 23 'a' chars uses major-type-3 with length encoded inline in the type byte (0x77 = 0x60 | 23). Boundary case before the 1-byte-length-prefix form.

vectors.name: long-string-24-bytes
vectors.doc: 24 'a' chars triggers the 1-byte-length-prefix form (0x78 0x18 + 24 bytes). Boundary above 23.

vectors.name: negative-integer-small
vectors.doc: Negative integer -1 encodes to 0x20 (major-type-1, value 0). CBOR negative-int encoding is -1 - n where n is the argument.

vectors.name: negative-integer-multibyte
vectors.doc: -100 encodes to 0x38 0x63 (major-type-1, 1-byte argument, value 99 -> -100).

vectors.name: byte-string
vectors.doc: Uint8Array([1,2,3]) encodes as major-type-2 length 3 (0x43) followed by the bytes.

vectors.name: array-positional
vectors.doc: Arrays preserve insertion order (positional, unlike objects which sort).

vectors.name: primitives
vectors.doc: null=0xf6, true=0xf5, false=0xf4 per RFC 8949 simple-value encoding inside a 3-element array.

vectors.name: mixed-shape
vectors.doc: Mixed object with 4 keys (n,b,s,a) inserted in NON-canonical order. Canonical sort by key bytes: a<b<n<s. Values exercise null, byte string, short string, and nested array of negative+zero ints.

vectors.name: integer-index-key-vs-empty-string
vectors.doc: Regression vector for the JS-engine integer-index-key reordering bug. Keys '' (empty string, 0x60) and '0' (one byte 0x6130). Canonical bytewise sort: '' (0x60) < '0' (0x6130). A plain JS object with these keys would enumerate '0' first because '0' is an array-index-canonical string per ECMA-262. The encoder MUST use a Map (or equivalent insertion-order-preserving carrier) so the canonical sort survives. Bit-exact output proves the carrier is correct.

vectors.name: integer-index-and-letter-key
vectors.doc: Mixed integer-like and letter keys. {a:1, '0':2}: canonical bytewise sort places '0' (0x6130) before 'a' (0x6161). A plain JS object enumerates ['0','a'] (array-index first), which happens to agree with canonical here, but only by coincidence; the previous vector locks the actual bug.

vectors.name: int-ladder-0
vectors.doc: Integer ladder, rung 1. the profile's shortest-form integer rule: smallest representation. 0 is inline in the head byte. Unchanged by the integer-widening rule; pinned so the ladder covers the whole range rather than only the range that moved.

vectors.name: int-ladder-23-last-inline
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. 23 is the last value carried inline in the head byte (additional info 0..23). Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-24-first-1-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. 24 is the first value needing a separate argument byte (additional info 24). Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-255-last-1-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. Last value expressible in a 1-byte argument. Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-256-first-2-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. First value needing a 2-byte argument (additional info 25). Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-65535-last-2-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. Last value expressible in a 2-byte argument. Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-65536-first-4-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. First value needing a 4-byte argument (additional info 26). Unchanged by the integer-widening rule.

vectors.name: int-ladder-4294967295-last-4-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder, THE BOUNDARY, low side. 2^32-1 is the last value the pre-widening encoder wrote as an integer at all. It must keep its 4-byte form: a fix that over-widened would push this to an 8-byte head and break shortest-form in the other direction.

vectors.name: int-ladder-4294967296-first-8-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder, THE BOUNDARY, high side. 2^32 needs an 8-byte argument (additional info 27). Before the integer-widening rule, this encoded as float64 fb41f0000000000000, contradicting the profile's shortest-form integer rule, RFC 8949 §4.2.2, and the profile's unsigned-integer grammar. Expected bytes derived from RFC 8949 §3.1 independently of cbor-x, and cross-checked against an independent downstream measurement naming 1b0000000100000000 as the post-fix expectation.

vectors.name: int-ladder-4294967297
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. 2^32+1, guarding against a fix that special-cases only the round boundary value.

vectors.name: int-ladder-max-safe-integer
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. 2^53-1, the top of this profile's integer value domain: the largest integer a JS number holds exactly.

vectors.name: int-ladder-negative-4294967296-last-4-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder, negative boundary, low side. Major type 1 encodes -1-n, so -(2^32) still fits a 4-byte argument (ffffffff) where the positive side has already run out. The negative boundary therefore sits one value further from zero than the positive one, which is exactly the off-by-one a naive symmetric fix gets wrong.

vectors.name: int-ladder-negative-4294967297-first-8-byte-arg
vectors.doc: Integer ladder, negative boundary, high side. -(2^32)-1 is the first negative value needing an 8-byte argument. Before the integer-widening rule, this encoded as float64 fbc1f0000000100000.

vectors.name: int-ladder-min-safe-integer
vectors.doc: Integer ladder. -(2^53-1), the bottom of the integer value domain. Major type 1 argument is -1-n = 2^53-2 = 001ffffffffffffe.

vectors.name: int-action-time-timestamp
vectors.doc: the integer-widening rule. A real Action.time in milliseconds since the epoch, the value that makes this defect universal: every Action carries one and every one of them is above 2^32. Before the integer-widening rule, this encoded as float64 fb4279ff1610b3d000.

vectors.name: int-grant-expires-at-in-map
vectors.doc: the integer-widening rule. The delegation grammar declares the grant expiry as an unsigned integer; it was historically pinned as a float64 and the fix was deferred to this profile. Pinned inside a map so the widening is proven in a structural position, not only as a bare top-level value.

vectors.name: int-above-safe-range-stays-float64
vectors.doc: the integer-widening rule negative-space vector. 2^53 is integral as a JS double but is NOT an exact integer in this profile's value domain, and the profile's shortest-form integer rule forbids tag 2/3 bignum, so no integer head can carry it. It therefore stays a float64, exactly as before the widening rule (confirmed 2026-08-11). Pinning it stops a future widening from quietly claiming integer precision the double does not have.

vectors.name: int-far-above-safe-range-stays-float64
vectors.doc: the integer-widening rule negative-space vector. 1e21 satisfies Number.isInteger but exceeds even uint64, so it could only be an integer via the forbidden bignum tag. Stays float64.

vectors.name: int-near-boundary-non-integer-stays-float64
vectors.doc: the integer-widening rule negative-space vector. 4294967296.5 sits just past the boundary in magnitude but is not an integer, so the widening must not touch it.

vectors.name: float-double-1.5
vectors.doc: Floating-point 1.5 encodes as IEEE 754 double-precision (CBOR major-type-7 simple-value 27 = 0xfb) followed by 8 big-endian bytes 0x3ff8000000000000. The encoder's alwaysUseFloat=false option keeps integers as integer-major-type while preserving float bit-exactness for non-integer numbers.

vectors.name: float-zero-half
vectors.doc: Floating-point 0.5 encodes as 0xfb 0x3fe0000000000000.
